table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: 91D1206000 (cal ID MB431M, JDM, 384kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

table.name: Gear 1 Slip Comp Pressure B
Gear 1 Slip Comp Pressure B (Accelerator pedal angle x256 minus reference speed (raw))

table.description: Gear 1 of 5. Pressure/duty correction curve. The X-input is (accelerator pedal angle x 256) minus the Reference Speed Baseline lookup — a difference, so the axis itself is raw even though both operands are now identified. Pedal angle arrives on CAN 0x412 byte 0 as raw 0-255 = 0-100%. Stock values are flat (20) in every gear.

table.name: CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve
CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

table.description: X-input is CAN ID 0x511 payload byte 4, scaled by a fixed 333/256 (~x1.301) factor before this lookup. CAN 0x511 originates from the VDC/ABS module (bytes 0-1 are steering wheel angle, byte 6 vehicle G-force); byte 4 is not identified in the community CAN decoding. Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

table.name: Gear Ratios (1st-5th)
table.description: The transmission's five forward gear ratios, indexed by current gear. Stock values match the Subaru factory service manual exactly: 3.540, 2.264, 1.471, 1.000, 0.834. The scale factor (raw/1024) is CONFIRMED — the decompiled code divides these by 0x400 when computing expected speed, and the result matches the published ratios to within 0.0007. Used by the TCU to compute expected output speed per gear and to detect gear-ratio faults (DTC P0730). Changing these does NOT change the physical gearing — it changes what the TCU BELIEVES the gearing is, which affects ratio-based fault detection and speed calculations.

table.name: Shift State Bit Pattern 1 of 5
table.description: One of five parallel 14-entry bit-pattern arrays (packed contiguously at 0x0087AA-0x0087EF), all indexed by the same internal shift-state variable (0-13) and each driving a different control output (this one feeds RAM 0x00808885). Confirmed via decompilation. EXPERT/DANGEROUS. These are BIT PATTERNS (every stock value is a power of two), not scalar quantities — editing them as ordinary numbers is very likely to produce an invalid pattern. On an automatic transmission an invalid clutch/solenoid pattern can command two elements at once, which can bind the driveline and cause real mechanical damage. The exact output each bit drives is NOT decoded — do not change these unless you have independently confirmed what each bit does on this exact firmware.

table.name: Cold ATF 5th Gear Lockout Temperature
table.description: Below this ATF temperature the TCU swaps in a placeholder (disabled) shift schedule specifically when in 5th gear — i.e. it restricts 5th until the fluid warms up. Stock 15 °C / 59 °F. Confirmed via decompilation: the check is gated on current gear == 5th. Raising it keeps 5th locked out longer; lowering it releases 5th sooner on a cold transmission.

table.name: Assumed ATF Temperature (Sensor Fallback)
table.description: The temperature the TCU substitutes when the measured ATF temperature is flagged unusable. Stock 95 °C / 203 °F — a deliberately warm assumption, so a failed sensor does not make the TCU behave as if the fluid were cold.

table.name: Cold Switchover Temperature (Lower)
table.description: Lower half of a two-point temperature switch with built-in hysteresis (pairs with 'Cold Switchover Temperature (Upper)'). Below this the TCU selects one calibration constant; at or above the upper point it selects another. Stock -10 °C / 14 °F.

table.name: Cold Switchover Temperature (Upper)
table.description: Upper half of the cold switchover hysteresis pair. Stock -5 °C / 23 °F. Keep this above the lower point — inverting them would remove the hysteresis and can cause the selection to chatter.

table.name: Speed Sensor 1 Pulses Per Revolution
table.description: Pulses per revolution for speed sensor channel 1. CONFIRMED: the firmware computes RPM as 60,000,000 / (this value x measured pulse period) — the standard period-to-RPM formula (60 seconds x a 1 MHz timer). Stock value 16, i.e. a 16-tooth tone ring. Change this ONLY if the physical tone ring / sensor tooth count actually differs, otherwise every speed-derived calculation in the TCU will be wrong.

table.name: Speed Sensor 2 Pulses Per Revolution
table.description: Pulses per revolution for speed sensor channel 2 — same confirmed 60,000,000/(N x period) RPM formula as channel 1, on an independent input with its own tooth count. Stock value 22. Same warning: only change this if the physical tooth count genuinely differs.

table.name: Speed Signal Ceiling (RPM)
table.description: Upper clamp applied to both speed-sensor channels AND to the CAN-received engine speed signal — all three are limited to this value. Stock 10000 (RPM). This shared clamp is part of the evidence that all three signals carry the same unit; it also sets the ceiling the engine-speed table axes are derived against.

table.name: Signal Smoothing Filter Gain (CAN 0x410 Chain)
table.description: Confirmed via decompilation: the calibratable gain argument to the first-order smoothing filter that produces the CAN ID 0x410-derived reference signal (docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md), stock value 128. Larger = faster response to changes in the incoming CAN signal, smaller = more smoothing/lag.

table.name: Signal Smoothing Filter Gain (Signal FE Chain)
table.description: Confirmed via decompilation: the calibratable gain argument to the smoothing filter that feeds the 'Smoothed Signal Response Curve' table (0x0117BE), stock value 128. Larger = faster response, smaller = more smoothing/lag.

table.name: Gear Threshold Constant
table.description: Confirmed via decompilation: a single-byte constant (stock value 2) compared directly against the current gear (0x0080885A) and a second gear-like index (0x0080886E) in several places in the same function — reads like a 'this logic only applies above/below gear N' cutoff. Exact effect of changing it is NOT verified on real hardware.

table.name: Signal Threshold Constant
table.description: Confirmed via decompilation: a constant compared against a computed signal delta in the same fault-detection routine that reads the Pressure Threshold E tables. Storage width (byte vs. word) was inferred from the surrounding code pattern, not independently double-checked — verify before relying on the exact stored value.

table.name: Temp Sensor 1 Linearisation
table.description:
ADC-to-temperature curve for temperature sensor 1. Column 1 is the inverted raw ADC reading, column 2 the resulting temperature as (value - 40) degrees C. This is the calibration that defines what the sensor reads: editing it changes every temperature-dependent decision the TCU makes. Confirmed encoding.
Format: each row is one segment, 4 x uint16. Column 1 is the breakpoint; columns 2-4 are the values interpolated across it. Rows chain (a row's later columns repeat the next row's earlier ones), so keep them consistent when editing. The final row is a max clamp.
Values are raw: no confirmed real-world conversion for this curve.

table.name: Temp Sensor 2 Linearisation
table.description:
ADC-to-temperature curve for temperature sensor 2. Same encoding as sensor 1: column 1 inverted raw ADC, column 2 temperature as (value - 40) degrees C.
Format: each row is one segment, 4 x uint16. Column 1 is the breakpoint; columns 2-4 are the values interpolated across it. Rows chain (a row's later columns repeat the next row's earlier ones), so keep them consistent when editing. The final row is a max clamp.

table.name: Shift 1-2 Upshift Curve
table.description:
Shift point curve, mode 0 (the fully-populated operating mode). Each row is one segment of a polyline in vehicle-speed / accelerator-angle space: the TCU shifts when the operating point crosses this line.
Columns: 1 = speed at the start of the segment, 2 = pedal angle at the start, 3 = speed at the end, 4 = pedal angle at the end. Column 3 of a row repeats column 1 of the next row, and column 4 repeats column 2 - KEEP THEM IN SYNC when editing or the curve will break.
Units are confirmed against the factory shift chart: speed is km/h directly, pedal angle is raw 0-255 shown here as 0-100%. A pedal value of 255 in the final row is a max clamp, not a real 100% point.
Lowering a curve makes that shift happen earlier (at lower speed for a given pedal); raising it delays the shift.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: 91FE216300 (cal ID MB436G, USDM, 512kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

table.name: CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve
CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

table.description: X-input is CAN ID 0x511 payload byte 4, scaled by a fixed 333/256 (~x1.301) factor before this lookup. CAN 0x511 originates from the VDC/ABS module (bytes 0-1 are steering wheel angle, byte 6 vehicle G-force); byte 4 is not identified in the community CAN decoding. Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

table.name: Temp Sensor 1 Linearisation
table.description:
ADC-to-temperature curve for temperature sensor 1. Column 1 is the inverted raw ADC reading, column 2 the resulting temperature as (value - 40) degrees C. This is the calibration that defines what the sensor reads: editing it changes every temperature-dependent decision the TCU makes. Confirmed encoding.
Format: each row is one segment, 4 x uint16. Column 1 is the breakpoint; columns 2-4 are the values interpolated across it. Rows chain (a row's later columns repeat the next row's earlier ones), so keep them consistent when editing. The final row is a max clamp.
Values are raw: no confirmed real-world conversion for this curve.

table.name: Shift 1-2 Upshift Curve
table.description:
Shift point curve, mode 0 (the fully-populated operating mode). Each row is one segment of a polyline in vehicle-speed / accelerator-angle space: the TCU shifts when the operating point crosses this line.
Columns: 1 = speed at the start of the segment, 2 = pedal angle at the start, 3 = speed at the end, 4 = pedal angle at the end. Column 3 of a row repeats column 1 of the next row, and column 4 repeats column 2 - KEEP THEM IN SYNC when editing or the curve will break.
Units are confirmed against the factory shift chart: speed is km/h directly, pedal angle is raw 0-255 shown here as 0-100%. A pedal value of 255 in the final row is a max clamp, not a real 100% point.
Lowering a curve makes that shift happen earlier (at lower speed for a given pedal); raising it delays the shift.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: 91D0207500 (cal ID MB436T, JDM, 384kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

table.description: X-input is CAN ID 0x511 payload byte 4, scaled by a fixed 333/256 (~x1.301) factor before this lookup. Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

table.name: Temp Sensor 1 Linearisation
table.description:
ADC-to-temperature curve for temperature sensor 1. Column 1 is the inverted raw ADC reading, column 2 the resulting temperature as (value - 40) degrees C. This is the calibration that defines what the sensor reads: editing it changes every temperature-dependent decision the TCU makes. Confirmed encoding.
Format: each row is one segment, 4 x uint16. Column 1 is the breakpoint; columns 2-4 are the values interpolated across it. Rows chain (a row's later columns repeat the next row's earlier ones), so keep them consistent when editing. The final row is a max clamp.
Values are raw: no confirmed real-world conversion for this curve.

table.name: Shift 1-2 Upshift Curve
table.description:
Shift point curve, mode 0 (the fully-populated operating mode). Each row is one segment of a polyline in vehicle-speed / accelerator-angle space: the TCU shifts when the operating point crosses this line.
Columns: 1 = speed at the start of the segment, 2 = pedal angle at the start, 3 = speed at the end, 4 = pedal angle at the end. Column 3 of a row repeats column 1 of the next row, and column 4 repeats column 2 - KEEP THEM IN SYNC when editing or the curve will break.
Units are confirmed against the factory shift chart: speed is km/h directly, pedal angle is raw 0-255 shown here as 0-100%. A pedal value of 255 in the final row is a max clamp, not a real 100% point.
Lowering a curve makes that shift happen earlier (at lower speed for a given pedal); raising it delays the shift.

table.name: Shift 3-4 Upshift Curve
table.description:
Shift point curve, mode 0 (the fully-populated operating mode). Each row is one segment of a polyline in vehicle-speed / accelerator-angle space: the TCU shifts when the operating point crosses this line.
Columns: 1 = speed at the start of the segment, 2 = pedal angle at the start, 3 = speed at the end, 4 = pedal angle at the end. Column 3 of a row repeats column 1 of the next row, and column 4 repeats column 2 - KEEP THEM IN SYNC when editing or the curve will break.
Units are confirmed against the factory shift chart: speed is km/h directly, pedal angle is raw 0-255 shown here as 0-100%. A pedal value of 255 in the final row is a max clamp, not a real 100% point.
Lowering a curve makes that shift happen earlier (at lower speed for a given pedal); raising it delays the shift.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: 91F0217100 (cal ID MB436P, USDM, 384kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

table.name: CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve
CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

table.description: X-input is CAN ID 0x511 payload byte 4, scaled by a fixed 333/256 (~x1.301) factor before this lookup. CAN 0x511 originates from the VDC/ABS module (bytes 0-1 are steering wheel angle, byte 6 vehicle G-force); byte 4 is not identified in the community CAN decoding. Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

table.name: Temp Sensor 1 Linearisation
table.description:
ADC-to-temperature curve for temperature sensor 1. Column 1 is the inverted raw ADC reading, column 2 the resulting temperature as (value - 40) degrees C. This is the calibration that defines what the sensor reads: editing it changes every temperature-dependent decision the TCU makes. Confirmed encoding.
Format: each row is one segment, 4 x uint16. Column 1 is the breakpoint; columns 2-4 are the values interpolated across it. Rows chain (a row's later columns repeat the next row's earlier ones), so keep them consistent when editing. The final row is a max clamp.
Values are raw: no confirmed real-world conversion for this curve.

table.name: Shift 1-2 Upshift Curve
table.description:
Shift point curve, mode 0 (the fully-populated operating mode). Each row is one segment of a polyline in vehicle-speed / accelerator-angle space: the TCU shifts when the operating point crosses this line.
Columns: 1 = speed at the start of the segment, 2 = pedal angle at the start, 3 = speed at the end, 4 = pedal angle at the end. Column 3 of a row repeats column 1 of the next row, and column 4 repeats column 2 - KEEP THEM IN SYNC when editing or the curve will break.
Units are confirmed against the factory shift chart: speed is km/h directly, pedal angle is raw 0-255 shown here as 0-100%. A pedal value of 255 in the final row is a max clamp, not a real 100% point.
Lowering a curve makes that shift happen earlier (at lower speed for a given pedal); raising it delays the shift.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: ABD1A03100 (cal ID MB4434, JDM, 384kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

table.description: X-input is CAN ID 0x511 payload byte 4, scaled by a fixed 333/256 (~x1.301) factor before this lookup. CAN 0x511 originates from the VDC/ABS module (bytes 0-1 are steering wheel angle, byte 6 vehicle G-force); byte 4 is not identified in the community CAN decoding. Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

Columns: 1 = speed at the start of the segment, 2 = pedal angle at the start, 3 = speed at the end, 4 = pedal angle at the end. Column 3 of a row repeats column 1 of the next row, and column 4 repeats column 2 - KEEP THEM IN SYNC when editing or the curve will break.
Units are confirmed against the factory shift chart: speed is km/h directly, pedal angle is raw 0-255 shown here as 0-100%. A pedal value of 255 in the final row is a max clamp, not a real 100% point.
Lowering a curve makes that shift happen earlier (at lower speed for a given pedal); raising it delays the shift.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: 91D1207900 (cal ID MB4373, JDM, 384kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

table.name: CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve
CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

table.description: X-input is CAN ID 0x511 payload byte 4, scaled by a fixed 333/256 (~x1.301) factor before this lookup. CAN 0x511 originates from the VDC/ABS module (bytes 0-1 are steering wheel angle, byte 6 vehicle G-force); byte 4 is not identified in the community CAN decoding. Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

table.name: Temp Sensor 1 Linearisation
table.description:
ADC-to-temperature curve for temperature sensor 1. Column 1 is the inverted raw ADC reading, column 2 the resulting temperature as (value - 40) degrees C. This is the calibration that defines what the sensor reads: editing it changes every temperature-dependent decision the TCU makes. Confirmed encoding.
Format: each row is one segment, 4 x uint16. Column 1 is the breakpoint; columns 2-4 are the values interpolated across it. Rows chain (a row's later columns repeat the next row's earlier ones), so keep them consistent when editing. The final row is a max clamp.
Values are raw: no confirmed real-world conversion for this curve.

table.name: Shift 1-2 Upshift Curve
table.description:
Shift point curve, mode 0 (the fully-populated operating mode). Each row is one segment of a polyline in vehicle-speed / accelerator-angle space: the TCU shifts when the operating point crosses this line.
Columns: 1 = speed at the start of the segment, 2 = pedal angle at the start, 3 = speed at the end, 4 = pedal angle at the end. Column 3 of a row repeats column 1 of the next row, and column 4 repeats column 2 - KEEP THEM IN SYNC when editing or the curve will break.
Units are confirmed against the factory shift chart: speed is km/h directly, pedal angle is raw 0-255 shown here as 0-100%. A pedal value of 255 in the final row is a max clamp, not a real 100% point.
Lowering a curve makes that shift happen earlier (at lower speed for a given pedal); raising it delays the shift.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: AAD1A07100 (cal ID MB440X, JDM, 384kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

table.name: Temp Sensor 1 Linearisation
table.description:
ADC-to-temperature curve for temperature sensor 1. Column 1 is the inverted raw ADC reading, column 2 the resulting temperature as (value - 40) degrees C. This is the calibration that defines what the sensor reads: editing it changes every temperature-dependent decision the TCU makes. Confirmed encoding.
Format: each row is one segment, 4 x uint16. Column 1 is the breakpoint; columns 2-4 are the values interpolated across it. Rows chain (a row's later columns repeat the next row's earlier ones), so keep them consistent when editing. The final row is a max clamp.
Values are raw: no confirmed real-world conversion for this curve.

table.name: Temp Sensor 2 Linearisation
table.description:
ADC-to-temperature curve for temperature sensor 2. Same encoding as sensor 1: column 1 inverted raw ADC, column 2 temperature as (value - 40) degrees C.
Format: each row is one segment, 4 x uint16. Column 1 is the breakpoint; columns 2-4 are the values interpolated across it. Rows chain (a row's later columns repeat the next row's earlier ones), so keep them consistent when editing. The final row is a max clamp.
Values are raw: no confirmed real-world conversion for this curve.

table.name: Shift 1-2 Upshift Curve
table.description:
Shift point curve, mode 0 (the fully-populated operating mode). Each row is one segment of a polyline in vehicle-speed / accelerator-angle space: the TCU shifts when the operating point crosses this line.
Columns: 1 = speed at the start of the segment, 2 = pedal angle at the start, 3 = speed at the end, 4 = pedal angle at the end. Column 3 of a row repeats column 1 of the next row, and column 4 repeats column 2 - KEEP THEM IN SYNC when editing or the curve will break.
Units are confirmed against the factory shift chart: speed is km/h directly, pedal angle is raw 0-255 shown here as 0-100%. A pedal value of 255 in the final row is a max clamp, not a real 100% point.
Lowering a curve makes that shift happen earlier (at lower speed for a given pedal); raising it delays the shift.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: ABD1207000 (cal ID MB5300, JDM, 384kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

table.name: CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve
CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

table.description: X-input is CAN ID 0x511 payload byte 4, scaled by a fixed 333/256 (~x1.301) factor before this lookup. CAN 0x511 originates from the VDC/ABS module (bytes 0-1 are steering wheel angle, byte 6 vehicle G-force); byte 4 is not identified in the community CAN decoding. Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

table.name: Shift 1-2 Upshift Curve
table.description:
Shift point curve, mode 0 (the fully-populated operating mode). Each row is one segment of a polyline in vehicle-speed / accelerator-angle space: the TCU shifts when the operating point crosses this line.
Columns: 1 = speed at the start of the segment, 2 = pedal angle at the start, 3 = speed at the end, 4 = pedal angle at the end. Column 3 of a row repeats column 1 of the next row, and column 4 repeats column 2 - KEEP THEM IN SYNC when editing or the curve will break.
Units are confirmed against the factory shift chart: speed is km/h directly, pedal angle is raw 0-255 shown here as 0-100%. A pedal value of 255 in the final row is a max clamp, not a real 100% point.
Lowering a curve makes that shift happen earlier (at lower speed for a given pedal); raising it delays the shift.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: ACD1207000 (cal ID MB558D01, JDM, 512kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

Columns: 1 = speed at the start of the segment, 2 = pedal angle at the start, 3 = speed at the end, 4 = pedal angle at the end. Column 3 of a row repeats column 1 of the next row, and column 4 repeats column 2 - KEEP THEM IN SYNC when editing or the curve will break.
Units are confirmed against the factory shift chart: speed is km/h directly, pedal angle is raw 0-255 shown here as 0-100%. A pedal value of 255 in the final row is a max clamp, not a real 100% point.
Lowering a curve makes that shift happen earlier (at lower speed for a given pedal); raising it delays the shift.

table.name: Read This First
table.description:
Firmware: ADE0236000 (cal ID MB562EH, Unknown, 512kb)
Subaru 5EAT TCU (5-speed automatic transmission control unit), Mitsubishi/Renesas M32R CPU.
Firmware: 91D1206000 (MB431M / R9H)
Origin: JDM TCU, MCU wa12212953www (M32R, 144-pin, 384KB). Most likely a 2003-2004 JDM Legacy — the market is stated by the person who dumped it, but the exact year/model is NOT confirmed (the unit had no housing or part-number label). Note this is NOT the 05-06 USDM TCU, which uses a different MCU.
Confirmed: table addresses, DTC list, checksum, gear ratios (raw/1024), Confirmed conversions: gear ratios (raw/1024), engine speed (raw/8), temperature (raw-40 degC), vehicle speed (km/h), accelerator pedal angle (raw/255 = 0-100%). Anything left as "raw" has no confirmed conversion. Pressure units are NOT confirmed and are not stored in the ROM. See docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md for detail.
REQUIRES RomRaider 1.0.0 or later. The shift schedule and record curves are 3D tables; RomRaider 0.8.2 reports "There was an error loading table" for them.
This is a static file editor only — cannot connect live to the vehicle through RomRaider. Run tools/checksum.py after any edit, before flashing.

table.name: Mode 1 Pressure Threshold E
Mode 1 Pressure Threshold E (Accelerator pedal angle x256 minus reference speed (raw))

table.description: Mode 1 of 2 (selected by an internal mode flag, not gear). Same slip-amount X-formula as Pressure Control B/C/D (confirmed via decompilation: X = smoothed reference * 256 - Reference Speed Baseline lookup). Stock data is flat (0) in both modes — a real, editable table even though it isn't currently varying.

table.name: Mode 2 Pressure Threshold E
Mode 2 Pressure Threshold E (Accelerator pedal angle x256 minus reference speed (raw))

table.description: Mode 2 of 2 (selected by an internal mode flag, not gear). Same slip-amount X-formula as Pressure Control B/C/D (confirmed via decompilation: X = smoothed reference * 256 - Reference Speed Baseline lookup). Stock data is flat (0) in both modes — a real, editable table even though it isn't currently varying.

table.name: CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve
CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

table.description: X-input is CAN ID 0x511 payload byte 4, scaled by a fixed 333/256 (~x1.301) factor before this lookup. CAN 0x511 originates from the VDC/ABS module (bytes 0-1 are steering wheel angle, byte 6 vehicle G-force); byte 4 is not identified in the community CAN decoding. Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

CAN 0x511 Byte 4 Threshold Curve (CAN 0x511 byte 4 (from VDC/ABS), raw x1.301)

Stock data is flat (0) — real, editable, currently inert.

table.name: Gear 1 Shift Correction
table.description:
Gear 1 of 5. Signed correction curve against engine speed, selected by a gear-indexed pointer array at 0x117A0. Gear 1 is all zeros (no correction), and the magnitude falls with each higher gear (about -1970 at the top of gear 2 down to -390 in gear 5) — the shape of a shift-shock or torque-phase correction.
Values are genuinely NEGATIVE and stored as signed 16-bit. Real-world units are not confirmed.
This family was only found after correcting the Ghidra M32R processor definition: the pointer array that selects it was unreadable before.

table.name: CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve
CAN 0x410 Chain Response Curve (Reference signal breakpoint (raw, pre-scale CAN 0x410 chain value))

table.description: X-input confirmed via decompilation: the same ceiling-clamped CAN ID 0x410-derived reference value already traced in docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md (before its x256 scale-up), NOT gear-indexed — a single standalone curve. Stock data is a genuine hump shape: rises from 61 to a peak of 127 around the middle of the axis, then falls back to 0 at the high end — a real, currently-populated tunable curve.

table.name: Signal FE Response Curve
Signal FE Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, source not fully traced))

table.description: X-input is an internal RAM value (traced back through several conditional assignments in the decompiled code, but not yet to a specific sensor or CAN ID — see docs/TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Stock data is a real, populated step curve (64 up to 256), not flat/placeholder.

table.name: Smoothed Signal Response Curve
Smoothed Signal Response Curve (Internal signal breakpoint (raw, x256 of a 0-255 byte))

table.description: X-input is the same internal signal as the 'Signal FE Response Curve' table, but smoothed through a calibratable first-order filter before this lookup (confirmed via decompilation: the filter target is that byte shifted left 8, i.e. x256). This is a DIFFERENT signal chain from the engine-speed tables, so the RPM scale used on those does NOT apply here — left raw deliberately. Stock data is a real, populated rising curve (200 up to 1189).

table.name: Shift 1-2 Upshift Curve
table.description:
Shift point curve, mode 0 (the fully-populated operating mode). Each row is one segment of a polyline in vehicle-speed / accelerator-angle space: the TCU shifts when the operating point crosses this line.
Columns: 1 = speed at the start of the segment, 2 = pedal angle at the start, 3 = speed at the end, 4 = pedal angle at the end. Column 3 of a row repeats column 1 of the next row, and column 4 repeats column 2 - KEEP THEM IN SYNC when editing or the curve will break.
Units are confirmed against the factory shift chart: speed is km/h directly, pedal angle is raw 0-255 shown here as 0-100%. A pedal value of 255 in the final row is a max clamp, not a real 100% point.
Lowering a curve makes that shift happen earlier (at lower speed for a given pedal); raising it delays the shift.
